Stated Claim / Post Context:
Higher-Page Jacobian and Albanese Tori

We construct, through Hodge-theoretical methods, what we call the $E_r$-Jacobian torus, the $E_r$-Albanese torus and the $E_r$-Albanese map of any compact complex manifold that is either {\it page-(r-1)-$\partial\bar\partial$} or {\it $E_r$-sGG}. These two classes of manifolds, the former of which is contained in the latter, have been introduced recently by both authors jointly with J. Stelzig, respectively by the first-named author. A Hodge theory is also developed for the latter class of manifolds. We then apply our results to give structure theorems and an identity of algebraic dimensions in terms of the $E_r$-Albanese map and torus. Other applications result in cohomological and metrical theorems for the $6$-dimensional sphere when it is equipped either with a hypothetical complex structure or with the complex structures very recently claimed to exist in the literature. For example, we show that in the latter case no {\it strongly Gauduchon} metric exists on $S^6$.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Albanese government's tough new rules to crack down on 'visa hopping' migrants

Those who abuse Australia's temporary migrant system by 'hopping from visa to visa' will face new roadblocks under new measures announced on Friday.

Actual Article Body:
By MAISY RAE - NEWS REPORTER and ANDREW BROWN FOR AAP

Published:  13:14 AEST, 2 October 2026   |  Updated:  13:48 AEST, 2 October 2026

People who abuse Australia's temporary migrant system by 'hopping from visa to visa' will face new roadblocks under rules proposed by the Albanese government.

From Friday, many international students and graduates will face new restrictions on bringing partners or children into Australia.

PhD students, foreign or Australian government scholarship holders and those from ASEAN or Pacific nations will be exempt, but will only be able to add dependants when their visa is granted.

Overseas students must also pay around $1,200 for a new visa if they want to change university courses, according to the new rules.
